subject: Post-call: Integration & Model Routing (SDK, Auth, Fallbacks) - Next steps
messages:

Subject: Post-call recap: Integration & model routing (SDK/auth/routing)

Hi Alex / Sreeni,

Thanks again for your time today - great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Summary of needs we heard:
  - SDK integration into your backend (Node/Python), service-to-service auth using short-lived keys.
  - Model routing rules: low-latency default for chat UI, cost-sensitive batch reranker for nightly jobs, and a controlled fallback chain for capacity events.
  - Structured output & tool-calling for order-extraction flows, plus embeddings/reranker pipeline for semantic search.

- Proposed immediate next steps:
  1) Technical deep-dive w/ your engs (45-60m) to go over SDK auth and sample routing config (Dev + Marcus to join).
  2) We'll share a sample model-routing YAML and a short SDK auth setup guide.
  3) Jointly define a small pilot: chat UI hooked to our low-latency route + nightly reranking job to validate cost/latency tradeoffs.

Ask: Can you share availability for a technical deep-dive Tue/Wed next week? Also please attach any internal constraints (e.g., must run in us-east-1 only, KMS/HSM requirements).

Attaching a short SDK-auth primer and a sample routing config we discussed.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Integration & model routing (SDK/auth/routing)

Thanks Marissa - this is super helpful. A couple of quick clarifications before we schedule the deep-dive: 

- Region constraint: for now we need inference to be within us-east-1 (data residency + latency). Is that straightforward with Redwood Dedicated or Private?
- KMS: our security team requires CMEK for model inputs/outputs. Can the SDK support token exchange to a customer-managed KMS?
- Fallback behavior: if low-latency pool is exhausted, we need automatic fallback to a slightly higher-latency model variant, but only for non-authenticated users. For authenticated sessions we prefer queuing (or retry) to maintain consistency. Can you share examples of routing policy syntax for this type of conditional fallback?

We'll get you availability for Tue/Wed next week.

- Alex
VP Product | Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 12:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Integration & model routing (SDK/auth/routing)

Hi Alex - great questions, answered inline below. Looping Dev and Marcus for the deep-dive and technical notes.

- Region constraint / deployment modes:
  - Hosted API: we have multi-region endpoints but for strict residency you can use Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity in us-east-1) or Private (customer VPC) depending on compliance needs. Both support pinning routes to a region.
  - Action: for the pilot, Dedicated in us-east-1 is the fastest to stand up if you want Redwood-managed infra. We'll include regional pinning in the sample config.

- KMS / CMEK:
  - We support integration with customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest and for key-wrapping of cached artifacts. For Private deployments we can plug into your HSM/KMS directly; for Dedicated we support bringing your KMS via a provisioning workflow (we'll share the checklist).
  - Action: security questionnaire + KMS whitepaper will be sent to your security contact.

- Routing / fallback policy syntax (example):
  - You can express conditional policies based on request attributes (auth: true/false), latency SLOs, and cost tiers. Example rule (high-level):

    - default-route: low-latency-gpt-16k (pinned to us-east-1)
    - on_capacity_exhaustion:
        if request.authenticated == true:
          action: queue_or_reject  # preserve deterministic outputs for auth users
        else:
          action: fallback_to: cost-optimized-gpt-8k

  - We'll provide a concrete YAML snippet in the deep-dive materials (see attached sample). Marcus / Dev: can you prepare a short snippet showing region pinning + auth-based fallback to bring to the call?

- Structured output & tool-calling: we support function/tool calling patterns and enforced structured schema outputs. For order extraction we recommend a schema-first approach + a small set of validators in the SDK. We can demo a tool-calling example that writes structured JSON to stdout and a validation step in the SDK that rejects malformed outputs.

- Embeddings/reranker pipeline: suggested pattern:
  1) Generate embeddings via a dedicated embeddings route (cheaper embeddings model).
  2) Reranker: run a lightweight reranker model (cost-optimized) against top-k candidates returned from vector search.
  3) Fallback: if reranker queue is backlogged, skip reranker and use a simpler lexical score with a confidence flag.

Next steps suggested:
- Dev technical deep-dive (45-60m): Proposed slots Wed 12/16 3pm PT or Thu 12/17 10am PT - can you confirm?
- Security team contact: send questionnaire and KMS checklist (we'll include in the follow-up email).
- Pilot definition: we'll draft a 2-week pilot plan after the deep-dive.

Thanks - Marcus and Dev will prepare the YAML snippets and SDK notes for auth/token exchange.

Best,
Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 11:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Integration & model routing (SDK/auth/routing) - Deep-dive prep + sample snippet

Alex / team - quick follow-up before the deep-dive. I attached a short sample YAML showing region pinning, auth-based fallback, and a cost/latency policy. Key notes:

- Region pinning: set "region: us-east-1" on the route block to ensure traffic stays in that region.
- Auth attribute: the SDK will send a request.metadata.authenticated boolean (true for users with active session tokens).
- Fallback chain: we model fallback as an ordered list of model variants with per-step actions (fallback, queue, or notify).

Sample (abridged):

route: chat_ui_low_latency
  region: us-east-1
  default_model: gpt-16k-lowlatency
  policies:
    - type: capacity
      on_exhaustion:
        - condition: request.metadata.authenticated == true
          action: queue
        - condition: request.metadata.authenticated == false
          action: fallback_to: gpt-8k-costopt
    - type: latency_slo
      p95_ms: 250

We'll walk through the full snippet in the call and show how to tune batching / KV cache policies for the chat flows to meet the p95 target.

Proposed call: Thu 12/17 10:00am PT - sending calendar invite now. Looking forward to the deep-dive.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
